title: ₹5 Crore Digital Bank Cyberattack: Complete Digital Forensic Investigation
businessProblem: ABC Digital Bank, a scheduled commercial banking entity, detected five critical anomalies: (1) An operations employee opened an obfuscated invoice attachment from a spoofed email; (2) High-value KYC and customer loan files were accessed and scrubbed from file servers; (3) The primary payment switch server initiated unauthorized outbound TCP connections to an overseas IP; (4) Customers logged ₹5 crore in fraudulent unauthorized outward RTGS/IMPS transactions; (5) Multiple branch workstations displayed LockBit ransomware lockscreens. The board suspects a coordinated insider-assisted advanced persistent threat (APT). Lead forensic investigators must rigorously identify evidence, maintain chain of custody, reverse-engineer disk and memory artifacts, analyze mobile and IoT logs, correlate cross-system timestamps into a super timeline, validate tool accuracy under NIST CFTT standards, and author a court-admissible forensic report distinguishing verified observations from hypotheses.

unitMapping.roleInSolution: Unit I (Preserve): First responder evidence triage across employee laptop, bank servers, smartphone, and network taps. Generation of cryptographic SHA-256 hashes, write-blocked bitstream imaging (.E01 / .raw), and physical chain of custody logs under Section 65B compliance.

Unit II (Recover): Examination of employee laptop NTFS Master File Table ($MFT), carving deleted customer Excel documents from unallocated clusters, and extraction of Windows execution artifacts (Prefetch, LNK, UserAssist, and Shellbags) proving malware launch.

Unit III (Reconstruct): Volatile memory triage of payment switch server with Volatility 3 (windows.pslist, windows.netscan, windows.malfind) uncovering unlinked process (PID 1220 unknown.exe) beaconing to 198.51.100.44:443, and building a 72-hour multi-source Super Timeline.

Unit IV (Examine Devices): Extraction of privileged employee's Android smartphone using logical backup and ADB file system acquisition; reverse-engineering WhatsApp and Signal SQLite databases; and parsing smart CCTV embedded memory for physical server room access.

Unit V (Validate & Report): Aggregating evidence into a master Evidence Register, conducting NIST CFTT validation checks, performing expert witness defense cross-examination simulation, and compiling an executive and court-ready Digital Forensic Investigation Report.

stepByStepProcess: Stage 1: Secure volatile state of banking switch (RAM dump via winpmem) and physical isolation of compromised subnets.
Stage 2: Acquire bitstream images of employee laptop using Tableau forensic write-blocker; verify SHA-256 integrity match.
Stage 3: File system analysis via Autopsy/TSK; identify deleted invoice 'Security_Update.pdf.exe' and carve deleted loan records.
Stage 4: Execute Volatility 3 plugins on switch memory dump; isolate injected DLL inside PID 1220 and trace outbound socket.
Stage 5: Parse Windows Event Logs (Security.evtx Event ID 4624, 4672, 7045) and correlate with NetFlow logs into Super Timeline.
Stage 6: Examine employee smartphone SQLite databases for suspicious SMS 2FA intercept codes and unauthorized remote access apps.
Stage 7: Conduct tool validation against NIST CFTT test references; audit limitations regarding attribution versus USB presence.
Stage 8: Synthesize final Forensic Report with defensible findings, chronology, and expert witness testimony prep.
expectedOutput: Root Cause Reconstruction: Adversary gained initial execution via spear-phishing macro on employee workstation at 08:42:15 UTC; executed lateral reconnaissance via SMB; established persistence on payment switch via service installation (PID 1220); routed ₹5 crore across 14 dummy recipient accounts at 14:15:00 UTC; deployed wiper/ransomware at 16:30:00 UTC to cover digital footprint.
practicalApplication: Production incident response protocols for financial institutions conforming to RBI Digital Payment Security Controls, CERT-In Cyber Incident Reporting standards, ISO/IEC 27037 digital evidence handling, and Indian Evidence Act Section 65B certification.
limitations: USB insertion artifact (Registry USBSTOR) proves physical connection and mount time, but does NOT independently prove data exfiltration without LNK or volume shadow corroboration.
Identical cryptographic hashes verify bitstream image integrity, but do not independently prove the identity or intent of the author.
Suspicious unlisted process names (e.g. unknown.exe) warrant memory analysis but cannot be declared malware without behavioral or binary disassembled proof.
Biometric fingerprint match on smartphone indicates authorized unlock mechanism, but cannot definitively prove whether the owner was acting under duress or voluntary action.
